 65% of Asian concertgoers have travelled overseas for shows, Trip.com Group & Live Nation study finds
 SPINS 
 800 
 Estimated:   reading 
 Words by Hidzir Junaini 
 First published: 5 November 2026 
 Last updated: 5 November 2026 
 News 
 Gigs 
 Events 
 Tech & Business 
 Concerts are no longer just an evening out. For a growing number of music fans across Asia, seeing their favourite artist live is reason enough to book a flight, pack a suitcase and explore an entirely new destination.
 According to The Concert Travel Effect in Asia , a new report released by Trip.com Group and Live Nation Asia on 4 November , 65% of concertgoers surveyed across six Asian markets have travelled to another country or region for a concert , highlighting the growing influence of live music on travel decisions.
 The research, which surveyed 1,768 respondents across Singapore, Mainland China, Hong Kong, Macao, Thailand and South Korea, also found that seven in 10 fans consider live music one of the most exciting reasons to travel.
 With major tours increasingly shaping travel itineraries, concert announcements are becoming just as important as holiday plans, particularly for fans willing to cross borders to catch their favourite acts.
 Singapore fans are travelling for music, while international acts drive visitors to the city
 In Singapore, 45% of concertgoers surveyed have travelled overseas for a concert , while 43% indicated that they would be willing to travel to South Korea to see an artist they really want to watch.
 South Korea emerged as the most popular potential concert travel destination among Singapore respondents, followed by Hong Kong and Macao (38%), Thailand (35%) and Mainland China (31%).
 The findings also highlight Singapore's growing appeal as a regional concert destination, with major international acts generating substantial interest from overseas audiences.
 Notably, flight bookings to Singapore surged by 203% within a day of Trip.com presales for The Weeknd's After Hours Til Dawn Tour , demonstrating how major concert ticketing events can coincide with sudden spikes in travel demand.
 K-pop continues to play a particularly significant role in attracting international concertgoers. According to Ticketmaster data included in the research, acts such as BTS and BLACKPINK generate some of the highest shares of overseas ticket demand in Singapore, ranging from 28% to 38%.
 Female fans from Mainland China and Southeast Asia were identified as the primary drivers of this cross-border demand for K-pop concerts in Singapore.
 The BTS effect: Concert announcements are sending flight bookings soaring
 The influence of K-pop extends well beyond Singapore.
 One striking example comes from the BTS WORLD TOUR 'ARIRANG' , which triggered a significant surge in regional travel bookings around its presale period.
 Within three days of Trip.com presales, flight bookings from Singapore to Bangkok increased by 200% , while bookings from Hong Kong to the Thai capital jumped by 309%.
 Across Trip.com's broader booking data, flights to Bangkok recorded an increase of more than 440% during the same presale window.
 The report also found that K-pop concerts in Bangkok attract nearly twice the share of overseas attendees compared to concerts by other acts, reinforcing the genre's ability to mobilise international fan communities.
 For many fans, however, securing a concert ticket is only the beginning of their travel plans.
 Among Singapore respondents, 64% identified securing concert tickets as the biggest factor driving their live music travel planning, followed by finding accommodation near the venue (50%) and affordable flights or transportation (48%).
 The findings suggest that tour announcements, ticket presales and general ticket sales are becoming increasingly important dates in the travel calendar.
 Concert trips are becoming longer, more premium experiences
 Rather than flying in solely for a performance, fans are increasingly turning concerts into extended holidays.
 Across the six markets, concertgoers indicated that they would ideally spend an average of four days at their destination. Singapore respondents expressed the strongest appetite for longer trips, with an ideal stay of 4.8 days .
 The research also revealed a growing preference for convenience and comfort.
 Some 84% of respondents across the region expressed interest in packages combining concert tickets with travel products, while 63% reported choosing five-star hotels when travelling for concerts.
 In Singapore specifically, 75% were interested in concert travel packages, with hotels (75%), flights (63%) and attractions or activities (42%) emerging as the most appealing additions.
 This demand is already translating into commercial growth.
 Since establishing their partnership in 2025, Trip.com Group and Live Nation Asia have offered packages combining concert access with accommodation, transport and local experiences.
 Bookings for these bundled ticket packages grew 64% year-on-year in the first half of 2026 , reflecting increasing interest in travel experiences built around live entertainment.
 Music fandom is changing the way people explore Asia
 Beyond the economic impact, the report highlights the increasingly social nature of concert travel.
 Across the six markets, two in three fans said their fan community was central to the concert experience, with younger audiences particularly enthusiastic about documenting and sharing their journeys on social media.
 This growing intersection of music, fandom and tourism is helping transform cities such as Singapore, Bangkok and Hong Kong into regional gathering points for fans.
 “A concert can make a city feel like somewhere a fan needs to be,” said James Dick , EVP of Partnerships and Media at Live Nation Asia.
 “Fans come for the artist, but they need a place to stay, they eat out and they explore while they’re there. One show can set a whole journey in motion.”
 For the live entertainment and tourism industries, the findings point to an increasingly interconnected future, where major concert tours influence not only ticket sales but also airline bookings, hotel demand and local tourism.
 And for music fans, the message is clear: sometimes, the best reason to visit a new city is simply knowing that your favourite artist will be there.
